items.title: The neighbourhoods where ADHD rates are skyrocketing
items.description: ADHD diagnoses in adults have exploded across Australia since 2017. For the first time, we have the data that shows where it is — and isn't — happening.

items.title: Australia faced the same dilemma as China in 2004 but made the wrong call
items.description: While the rest of us count the cost in higher fuel costs, higher inflation and a weaker economy,  China — the actual winner of the war — will be enjoying a surge of global interest in its solar panels, wind turbines and electric vehicles.

items.title: Iran daily briefing: Why JD Vance might have no-one to talk to, plus Israel's new 'yellow line'
items.description: Welcome to Monday and a return to the rhetorical threat spiral we've been watching for weeks. Here's what you should know this morning.

items.title: Live: Iran vows retaliation over ship attack; Australia's treasurer says economy in part 'hostage' to US, Iran moves
items.description: Iran's top joint military command accuses the US of violating a ceasefire by firing at an Iranian commercial ship in the Gulf of Oman and vows to retaliate. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Chalmers to hold talks with states as he flags further NDIS 'savings'
items.description: Treasurer Jim Chalmers is flagging more "savings" to the National Disability Insurance Scheme as the government seeks to curb growth to about 5 per cent. Follow live.

items.title: Breaking: ACT Greens leader Shane Rattenbury quitting politics
items.description: The leader of the ACT Greens and former attorney-general Shane Rattenbury has announced he is leaving politics after more than 17 years in the Legislative Assembly.

items.title: The government is looking for cuts and thinks it has found its target
items.description: For the first time in this survey, more Australians are dissatisfied with the direction of the country than satisfied. The conflict between the US/Israel and Iran has delivered more than geopolitical uncertainty.

items.title: The world is on the cusp of an 'era of extreme scarcity'. Enter Vladimir Putin
items.description: With fears hunger could hit record levels, Vladimir Putin and Russia are poised to capitalise — financially and diplomatically.

items.title: Price of groceries to increase within weeks due to war in Iran
items.description: Farmers ask for a 30-cent-per-litre price rise for milk as fuel and fertiliser prices surge.

items.title: Australia's biggest AI factory planned for remote WA
items.description: A huge artificial intelligence data centre capable of training models like ChatGPT is planned for WA's remote north at a cost of billons of dollars.

items.title: Dragons take aim at 'personal agendas' in the media as coach shown the door
items.description: Shane Flanagan and the St George Illawarra Dragons part ways after a winless start to 2026 extends an 11-game losing streak dating back to last August.

items.title: Grieving mother of Belgian backpacker warns hikers not to trust phone maps
items.description: Backpacker Celine Cremer set off on a short walk with only a phone to guide her — and vanished. More than two years later, her family has an urgent message for other travellers.

items.title: RSL denies services club's Anzac Day two-up request
items.description: An ex-services organisation wants changes to Queensland legislation that allows the local RSL branch to reject its application to play two-up on Anzac Day.

items.title: Live: Rising Hormuz tension has ASX on edge after Wall Street highs
items.description: Wall Street hit new highs while oil prices retreated sharply on hopes of a US-Iran peace deal on Friday. Those hopes are now fading. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Are you ever allowed to trim a council tree if it's near your property?
items.description: Expert advice on how to handle council trees causing problems on private property.

items.title: Quiz: Can you tame our tricky history questions?
items.description: Is two-up actually illegal in Australia? And what movie beat Crocodile Dundee to the top of the box office in 1986?

items.title: 'I had no-one to talk to': The 92yo trying to save his dying language
items.description: Peter is the last living speaker of the First Nations language Thiinma. When he met linguist Rosie, they used music to help keep his knowledge alive, and formed a beautiful friendship along the way.

items.title: Two-thirds of Australians leave private information open to cybercriminals
items.description: New research suggests Australians are leaving themselves vulnerable to cybercrime through their public social media accounts.

items.title: 'Hard to break the habit': Why free public transport isn't enough to shift from cars
items.description: Free public transport is a popular policy, but researchers say it's not enough to convince drivers to leave the car at home.

items.title: Touring musicians rethink careers as fuel prices bite
items.description: Adele Oliver admits being a country music artist has "never been a great career choice", but she says things are worse than ever, with her last gig costing her money due to the escalating price of fuel.

items.title: Thousands displaced as fire destroys homes on Malaysia's Borneo island
items.description: Thousands of people are displaced after a fire destroys about 1,000 homes in a coastal village in Malaysia's Sabah state, the fire department says.

items.title: US domestic violence shooting leaves eight children dead
items.description: The victims, who were shot at two homes in the US state of Louisiana, ranged in age from one to about 14 years old.

items.title: Profits shrivel as yellow tail winemaker posts $5.5 million loss
items.description: The maker of one of Australia's best-known wine brands, yellow tail, says rising costs and global factors such as tariffs are behind the sharp drop in profits.

items.title: Blood donation eligibility expands for gay and bisexual men, transgender people
items.description: From today, Australian Red Cross Lifeblood will use gender-neutral assessments for blood and platelets donations.

items.title: Man charged with stealing seven vehicles, including unmarked police car
items.description: A Shepparton man will face court accused of stealing seven cars in Melbourne and Victoria's north in March and April.
